title: “Glukoathletes": glucose uptake in trained individuals
summary:
The aim of the present study was to compare glucose clearance from the blood in athletes with different forms of training. The study distinguishes between between endurance athletes who have trained for many years, strength athletes and athletes who have carried out combined strength and endurance training for many years.  
The aim is to determine in which of the above training groups the glucose from the blood is cleared from the blood most effectively/fastest.  Highly trained athletes will be examined who have been active in one of these forms of training for at least three years. Outcomes are the capillary Δblood glucose value 30 min, 1h, 90 min, 2h in the oral glucose tolerance test after ingestion of 75 g glucose solution at time 0. In the analysis with groups matched as far as possible in age, gender, height and training time per week, the values should be evaluated directly as well as normalized to the muscle mass, which, as expected, should be relatively high in strength athletes in particular (glucose should be relatively high (glucose deletion per kg of muscle mass and in relation to relative muscle mass). 
muscle mass). In addition, the HOMA and HOMA-ß indices are determined for the assessment of insulin resistance and beta cell function and related to glucose deletion. 
The study should provide valuable insights into the glucose metabolism of athletes. This can be used to make more precise recommendations, for example for glucose administration before competitions or during training. The study results could also provide information on which forms of training are particularly suitable for people with prediabetes/diabetes in order to positively influence positively influence glucose tolerance in the long term.

Inclusion criteria:
Persons of male, female or diverse gender; age 18-30 years, training volume of 
endurance training, strength training or combined strength and endurance training of at least six hours/week for at least three 
hours/week for at least three years. For the groups that primarily do either 
endurance training or strength training, it is important that at least 80% of their weekly training 
training workload in the respective primary form of training. The group that 
combined strength training and endurance training may not exceed a difference of 20% between the two different forms of training. 
between the two different forms of strength training and endurance training.
Exclusion criteria:
Known chronic diseases (diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, high blood pressure, etc. and, if applicable, corresponding medication). 
corresponding medication). The diseases leading to exclusion include in particular 
known performance- or training-limiting illnesses of various kinds (cardiovascular diseases, e.g. uncontrollable heart
diseases, e.g. uncontrollable cardiac arrhythmia, heart failure (EF < 55), PAOD 
(Fontaine stage ≥ II), degenerative joint diseases or muscular diseases). 
Chronic gastrointestinal diseases, as the performance of the oral glucose tolerance test in the side effect profile can cause gastrointestinal problems. The following are also 
exclusion criteria: Smoking status, acute oncological diseases or a history of such diseases (< 5 years), infections (HIV, hepatitis), addictions, neurological disorders, psychiatric disorders, existing pregnancy. illnesses, existing pregnancy. The use of oral contraceptives (contraceptive pill) or thyroid preparations and painkillers also lead to exclusion.
